verses.text: I looked again at all the oppression happening under the sun. I saw the tears of the people being crushed, with nobody to comfort them. The people crushing them had all the power, and still there was nobody to comfort them.
So I counted those who'd been dead a long time better off than the people still alive.
Better off than either is the person who hasn't been born, who's never seen the evil people do under the sun.
Then I saw how all that hard work and achievement makes neighbors envy each other. That too slips away like a breath, like chasing the wind.
A fool folds their hands and lets their own life fall apart.
Better to have one handful and some peace than two handfuls that cost you endless work and leave you chasing the wind.
I looked again and saw something else slipping away under the sun.

Here's someone all alone, with no son or brother. Their work never ends, and they never see enough money to feel satisfied. “Who am I working for, then? Why am I cutting myself off from anything good?” That too slips away like a breath. What a miserable way to spend your life.
Two are better than one. They get a good return for the work they put in together.
If one falls, the other can help them up. But it's awful to fall when you're alone and nobody's there to lift you.
If two people lie down together, they can keep warm. How's one person supposed to stay warm alone?
Someone can overpower one person, but two can stand against them. A cord of three strands won't snap in a hurry.
A poor kid with wisdom is better than an old king who's too foolish to listen when someone corrects him.
That young man came out of prison to be king, even though he was born poor in that very kingdom.
I saw all the people walking under the sun side with the young man who took the older king's place.
There was no end to the crowd he ruled. But the people who come later won't celebrate him. That too slips away like a breath, like chasing the wind.
